deferred_decisions.issue: A `.git` at the store root is never treated as a unit, because the `base == store` branch runs first. The walk then enters `store/.git`, yields its `hooks/*` files, and hits the same `.git/hooks` mkdir denial. `prune_empty_dirs` also removes empty dirs inside it. This is unlikely, but it is the same crash class
deferred_decisions.reason: Repository at the tmp store root is outside nested-fixture scope; moving the store into its own trash is invalid. Separate refusal policy required.

autonomous_decisions.issue: Nothing tests the new unit guard in `prune_empty_dirs`. I swapped the pre-change prune back in and all 15 tests in `test_purge_devtmp.py` still pass. The guard matters: on a `git init` fixture that is classed fresh and kept in apply mode, the old prune deletes the empty `.git/refs` and `.git/objects` dirs, and `git rev-parse` then exits 128 with "not a git repository". Add an apply-mode test with a fresh unit that holds empty `.git/refs/heads` and `.git/objects/pack`, and assert they survive

Move the inner walk and its fallback into `newest_file_mtime(directory: Path) -> float`. The branch then becomes `yield Path(base).relative_to(store), newest_file_mtime(Path(base))`, `dirs[:] = []`, `continue`

autonomous_decisions.issue: `max(mtimes, default=Path(base).stat().st_mtime)` runs `stat` for every unit, even when files were found, and nothing catches its error. If another session deletes the unit during the inner walk, `FileNotFoundError` stops the whole store run. That is the failure this PRD set out to remove.
